title: Rice Pudding
subtitle: Creamy baked pudding rice with nutmeg
excerpt: Short-grain pudding rice baked slowly in whole milk and cream with sugar and nutmeg until thick, creamy, and golden on top. Best eaten warm with a spoonful of jam. A British pudding in the most comforting sense.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rice pudding has been eaten in Britain since the 17th century, when recipes appear in English cookery books. The method is straightforward: short-grain rice absorbs milk over a long, slow bake, becoming swollen and creamy. The characteristic skin that forms on top is a feature, not a flaw. Pudding rice is a short-grain variety specifically sold for this purpose; Arborio works as a substitute. The traditional accompaniment is a spoonful of raspberry or strawberry jam stirred in at the table.

recipeTools.notes: A medium oven-proof dish, roughly 25 x 18 cm.

content.text: Do not stir during cooking: disturbing the pudding prevents the skin from forming and can make the texture stodgy. The pudding needs a full 2 hours in a low oven. It is done when the rice has absorbed most of the liquid, the top is golden brown, and the pudding still wobbles slightly in the centre when the dish is shaken.
Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Butter an oven-proof dish.
Put the rice, milk, cream, sugar, and vanilla into the dish. Stir briefly to combine. Grate the nutmeg generously over the top. Dot with butter.
Bake for 2 hours without stirring. The skin should be golden brown and the pudding just set. Serve warm with a spoonful of raspberry jam.
